Kenneth decided on 2026-10-21, before any code: a calibration is a project of its own
("acceptable, as long as we have a way to tell user what will happen"); the first tests
are temperature, flow and pressure advance; a result is saved as a named filament copy
(as the printer panel saves with persistAs); the physical-print ledger "doesn't matter,
whatever is the easiest". Entry points: the printer chip menu, the filament slot menu and
the Home card kebab each get a "Calibrate…" row; a symptom in the project chat leads to
the same conversation. No code exists yet; the tool guide's `calibration_generate` row
("onto a new plate") is wrong and must be corrected when the tool is specified.

**Why (verified by reading, not running):** every `Plater::calib_*` generator (Plater.cpp
~12677-13650) calls `new_project()` and then edits the single edited print, filament and
printer presets (`preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`),
so a test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. The test
mode itself lives on the current plate's `Print` (`set_calib_params`), is read by
GCode.cpp per layer, is NOT written to the 3MF and is reset to Calib_None on load
(Plater.cpp:5891). A reopened tower slices at one temperature; the PA pattern is the
exception (its per-layer commands go into the plate's saved custom G-code) and it
hard-codes plate 0's origin.

(https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), page id `calibration`
("Calibration · Printer & Filament"), boards `calibration-01…08-*.dc.html`, generated by

Verified by running a throwaway `--calibration` mode of the real-adapter harness on jusprin-newui 14fe07a078 (report: `calibration-generate-verification.md`, untracked in worktree `kind-mestorf-a37ba6`; probe code and log in the side-session notes folder `calibration-generate-probe/`).

- No dialog in any case. But each generator's own `new_project()` gives JusPrin a new project id, workspace session and empty chat (`ProjectPersistence` starts a fresh identity when the aux dir moves).
- An empty project with a chat (doc_revision > 1) is saved by the release hook and shows on Home as its own project; an untouched one is not saved.
- `Plater::set_project_filename(bare name)` renames with no file side effects. The name only sticks if set before the first autosave capture, because `ProjectAutosave` fixes `m_project_name` at the first version.
- Temp, flow, PA pattern and PA tower results (objects, `calib_params`, preset edits, PA custom G-code) match Orca's own path exactly. Unsaved preset edits made in the empty project carry into the test, because the release hook skips Orca's keep/discard question.
- Trap: the PA pattern's G-code comments depend on the process-wide `GCodeWriter::full_gcode_comment`, which the first finished export sets. Pin it before comparing two runs.

**Why:** Kenneth's 2026-10-22 flow ("one popup → empty calibration project → agent asks which test → generate into this project") assumed the generator would reuse the open project.
**How to apply:** do not add an Orca seam. The proposal is fork-owned: a one-shot "continue this identity across the next boundary" in ProjectPersistence, the release hook skipping its save while it is armed, the tool calling calib_* under ToolLoad and renaming in the same call, plus a rule for AgentHost's session filter (AgentHost.cpp:715). Related: [[calibration-design-decisions]].

Keep an empty project in memory until it holds a model

OrcaSlicer always holds a project and starts with an empty one. JusPrin saved
that project as soon as its document changed, so a printer switch or a

A project now saves only when a model is present or it was saved before. A
chat, draft, setting edit or preset choice on an empty plate doesn't save it,

undoing its first import means deleting the object. pin_current tells the two

project.

straight away, because a model attachment needs a real file path. The folder
is removed when a never-saved project is left or the app exits, and kept across
a switch to classic view. A crash can leave one behind, with no HEAD and no card.

Home lists a project if any of its versions holds a model, so a project whose
objects were all deleted keeps its card. Older projects that never held a model
lose their card and stay on disk.

content.text:
No, this isn't how calibration is supposed to work. You decided the design between Oct 21 and 23, and commit `48c402949b` ("Calibrate a filament: one popup, a calibration project, a saved preset") built it. In that design you never land in an "Untitled" project with an empty chat.

**What should have happened**
1. You click "Calibrate…" in the printer menu, the filament menu or a Home printer card. A popup asks "Calibrate Bambu PLA Basic on Bambu Lab P1S?" and says two things: your open project will be saved and closed, and the test's settings are temporary. You click Start.
2. The app opens a new project named "Calibration · Bambu PLA Basic · Bambu Lab P1S". Its chat has the same name and starts with a note about where you came from. The AI talks first. It asks which test only when the reason you started doesn't already settle it, offering "Temperature tower", "Flow tiles" and "Pressure advance" as reply choices.
3. The AI makes the tower in that same project. The project keeps its name and its chat, and the AI tells you to print the tower and send a photo. Later it offers to save the best temperature as a new filament preset.

**Why the design cares about this.** OrcaSlicer's own temperature-tower generator always throws away the open project and starts a new blank one. Without a fix, JusPrin treats that as a brand-new project, with a new id, the name "Untitled" and an empty chat. A test run on Oct 22 confirmed this. One candidate is commit `74a0e9b61c` from Nov 2 ("Keep an empty project in memory until it holds a model"). It changed when an empty project first gets saved, and the 2.5.0 merge notes say it changed how the calibration project gets saved. I also can't tell which way you started the test, because the app's logs on this Mac have nothing from today's run. If OrcaSlicer's own Calibration menu showed up somewhere, the same symptom would appear. JusPrin is supposed to hide that menu while its own interface is on.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. - A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.

name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

content.text:
I reproduced the bug in the real app. When the AI makes the temperature tower, the calibration chat disappears and an empty "New chat" takes its place, just like your screenshot. I used a copy of the current `jusprin-dev` build (built at 12:17 today from commit `09083ec472`) with a copy of your normal data folder, and gave it its own app id so your running app was never touched.

**What I did and saw**
1. On Home, I clicked Printer › Calibrate…. The popup asked "Calibrate Generic PLA on Bambu Lab P1S (2)?" and I clicked Start.
2. The app opened a project named "Calibration · Generic PLA · Bambu Lab P1S (2)". Its chat had the handover line, and the AI asked what problem I was seeing, offering "Temperature tower", "Flow tiles" and "Pressure advance". All of this matches the design.
3. I clicked "Temperature tower" and the AI made the tower (240 °C down to 190 °C). The chat panel immediately switched to an empty "New chat", and the setup summary changed to "10 settings differ from the presets". The window title kept the calibration name. I've sent you before and after screenshots.

**What the saved data shows.** Only one new project was created, so the carry-over did keep a single project. But the chat inside it is new: its one conversation has no messages, and it was created at 17:15:32, the moment the tower was made, not at 17:14 when I clicked Start. The tower call is recorded in it as successful, so the tool's result landed in a chat with nothing before it. The AI's question and my "Temperature tower" reply are gone.

**Where the cause might be (not verified yet).** When the generator throws away the open project, `ProjectPersistence::continuing_project` is supposed to keep the in-memory chat. In this run the chat was rebuilt from scratch. My lead suspect is still commit `74a0e9b61c` (Nov 2, "Keep an empty project in memory until it holds a model"). Since that commit, the calibration project isn't saved until the tower is added, so some other code path may be resetting the chat. I haven't traced that yet.

**A second, smaller problem.** The model in your data folder (GPT-5.4 Mini) first called the tower tool without a temperature range. The app refused the call, and the AI showed "I hit a tool mismatch" before I pressed "Regenerate tower". That's about how the tool asks for its arguments, not the lost chat, and it may not happen with the "Expert" model you used.

The scratch copy is stopped. Its files are in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/ea795ba1-b280-4fa1-aeb7-b06d82baeefa/scratchpad/repro/`.
